newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian PM urges France to hand over Dassault info.
newsitem.headline: Belgian PM urges France to hand over Dassault info.

text.p: Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene is ready to intervene personally to put pressure on France to hand over information it has on allegations that a French defence firm bribed Belgian political parties.

Dehaene said in answer to a parliamentary question that France had so far not heeded a request from the Justice Ministry for documents in the case allegedly involving French group Dassault. Dassault has denied any wrongdoing.

He said the French attitude disappointed him, certainly against the backdrop of closer cooperation in legal and police matters between the two countries. He gave no indication of when he would act or who he would approach in the French government.
Last month a French court gave Belgian police some of the papers requested more than a year ago, after Justice Minister Stefaan De Clerck personally contacted his French counterpart Jacques Toubon.
About a week ago De Clerck asked the French to surrender the remaining papers, seized in 1995 and relating to a front company which Belgian police believe was used to pay the bribes.
The police are investigating allegations Dassault paid 600 million Belgian francs ($19 million) to parties to secure a 1989 contract to fit air defence systems to Belgian fighter jets.
The francophone socialist party (PS) has said it received what it called a legal gift of 1.2 million francs from Dassault in 1987 and acknowledged it had contacts with Dassault.
Belgium did not restrict corporate funding of political parties until 1989 and only banned it completely in 1993.
Police have so far unearthed several Luxembourg bank accounts and identified a total 42 million francs, traced to PS officials.

Two senior PS officials have been arrested in the Dassault case which has shaken the centre-left coalition, in which the PS is one of four partners, to the core. Dehaene, however, refuses to admit there is a crisis and is adamant on staying put.
